best_for: Network admins, security staff and developers who need to see the actual packets on a wire to find out why a connection fails or what an app sends.

points.title: Packet capture comes bundled
points.text: Each Windows installer includes the current Npcap, the driver needed for live capture, so one install is enough to start capturing.

points.title: Windows: 64-bit only
points.text: Wireshark 3.6 was the last branch for 32-bit Windows. It supports Windows 10 and 11 and Server 2016 to 2022, and wants 500 MB of free RAM and disk, more for large captures. This site lists x64 installers only; Arm64 builds are on wireshark.org.

points.title: One Mac app for both chips
points.text: The macOS download is a universal disk image for Intel and Apple silicon.

points.title: The Flatpak is a community build
points.text: The Flathub package is not marked verified by Flathub. The project's own Linux route is your distribution's packages, with a Launchpad repository for Ubuntu.

points.title: A portable option
points.text: A PortableApps package for Windows x64 is published with each release, for use without installing.

points.title: Free, and steep to learn
points.text: Wireshark is open source under the GPL-2.0. It shows a lot of detail, so expect to learn capture and display filters before it answers your question; the project's docs and Learn pages help.

points.title: Versions kept here
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 46 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
